This bill would keep several counter-terrorism powers in force beyond their current expiry date.
It extends control orders, preventative detention orders, declared areas rules, and stop-search-seize powers for three more years, and ASIO questioning powers for one more year.
The bill also updates the Criminal Code to assign responsibility for protecting sensitive information under the continuing detention order regime to the Attorney-General and the AFP Minister.

Counter-Terrorism Legislation Amendment Bill (No. 1) 2018 - Second Reading - Agree with bill's main idea

The bill extends the sunset date for control order, preventative detention order and declared area regimes to 7 September 2021. The government did not implement PJCIS and INSLM recommendations to repeal questioning and detention warrants and to exempt control order subjects from paying costs for variation applications.

The speaker argued for extending the control order sunset clause, raised concerns that police cannot question people under preventative detention orders (PDOs), and advocated for a national criminal intelligence database and community protection intervention orders to compel deradicalisation, citing around 500 persons of interest in Australia and examples such as Numan Haider and Abdul Nacer Benbrika.

The bill extends the control order, preventive detention order, declared areas, and terrorism stop/search/seizure powers for three years until 7 September 2021, and continues ASIO’s questioning and detention powers for 12 months, while also increasing independent oversight of these counter-terrorism provisions.
